title: OpenCode hack exposes API keys amid AI distillation attacks
content_md: The open-source AI coding project OpenCode has notified some users that stored API keys they used with external providers were exposed in a security breach. Multiple users reported that the incident led to unauthorized API charges and suspended projects in Google Cloud. According to the project maintainer, the breach affected 1.4% of OpenCode Console users, with some reporting more than $1,700 in unauthorized charges overnight. OpenCode is a model-agnostic AI coding agent that helps users understand code, write features, and fix bugs using natural-language instructions, through a terminal, desktop app, or code editor. Users can connect AI models from multiple AI providers to the OpenCode console to streamline and automate the development process. On Saturday, OpenCode announced that it suffered a large distillation attack that impacted only developers who linked external providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google. “We had a security breach last night related to a large-scale distillation attack that impacted 1.4% of OpenCode Console users,” the project maintainer said . “We have notified them all this morning via email. If you did not get an email, you were not impacted, it was a subset of users who had external providers linked.” Distillation is a legitimate machine-learning technique that trains smaller AI models using responses generated by more powerful models.
